title: Isolation and Characterization of Mouse Alveolar Bone Marrow Hematopoietic Stem Cells
author: Niizuma, Morikawa, et al.
materials: FSC-A vs. SSC-A to identify cells. (Gate

steps.title: Prepare buffers, reagents, and equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare and filter all required buffers, verify antibody expiration dates and optimal dilutions, ensure all materials and equipment are available, complete documentation, label tubes and plates, warm up flow cytometer lasers for at least 30 min, run cytometer performance validation with CS&T beads and check fluidics, prepare single‑stained and unstained compensation controls, test Propidium Iodide (PI) staining on control samples, and verify cell sorter function including drop‑delay calibration.

substeps.instruction: Prepare and filter all required buffers (see recipes).
Check expiration dates and optimal dilutions for all antibodies.
Ensure availability of all required materials and equipment.
Prepare experiment worksheets, data‑collection templates, and analysis protocols.
Label all tubes and plates clearly.
Warm up flow cytometer lasers for ≥30 min.
Run cytometer performance validation using CS&T beads and inspect fluidics.
Prepare compensation controls (single‑stained and unstained).
Test PI staining on control samples.
Verify cell sorter operation and perform drop‑delay calibration.

steps.title: Prepare FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 499.5 mL PBS with 0.5 mL Propidium Iodide (0.1 % final) to obtain 500 mL FACS buffer; store at 4 °C protected from light for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Isolate alveolar bone marrow
steps.instruction: Perform sterile dissection of the mouse mandible, isolate the alveolar bone region, and generate a single‑cell suspension while keeping all tissues on ice (0–4 °C).

substeps.instruction: Prepare sterile surgical tools (scissors, fine forceps, fine scissors) in a sterile field and place ice‑cold PBS (Gibco, Cat# 10010‑023) in a sterile tube.
Euthanize 8–12‑week‑old C57BL/6 mice by CO₂ inhalation followed by cervical dislocation according to institutional guidelines.
Make a lateral skin incision on the face, remove lower‑jaw skin, and open the mouth to expose the mandibular region.

Detach masticatory muscles from the mandible, remove major muscle groups, wipe residual tissue with Kimwipes, locate and detach the temporomandibular joint, and extract the intact mandible, keeping it on ice.
Identify the alveolar region between molar and incisor, dissect the alveolar bone with fine scissors while avoiding tooth roots and dental pulp.

Wash the isolated alveolar bone with ice‑cold PBS, crush the bone using a mortar and pestle, filter the resulting suspension through a 70‑µm cell strainer (Falcon, Cat# 352350), centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, and resuspend the pellet in PBS. No red‑blood‑cell lysis is performed. The suspension can be kept on ice for up to 1 h before the next step.

steps.title: Stain cells and prepare antibody cocktail
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension, adjust cell concentration, add lineage cocktail, incubate, wash, add fluorochrome‑conjugated antibodies at specified dilutions, and incubate for 90 min on ice in the dark.

substeps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension through a 40‑µm cell strainer to remove remaining bone fragments.
Count cells with a hemocytometer and adjust to 1–5 × 10⁶ cells/mL in cold FACS buffer.
Transfer cells to 5‑mL FACS tubes.
Add lineage‑cocktail antibodies (3 µL per 1 × 10⁷ cells).

Prepare the lineage‑cocktail master mix (store at 4 °C protected from light, up to 3 months):
   • Biotin‑Gr1/Ly‑6G 0.5 mg/mL – 100 µL
   • Biotin‑Ter119 0.5 mg/mL – 100 µL
   • Biotin‑CD40 0.5 mg/mL – 25 µL
   • Biotin‑CD80 0.5 mg/mL – 25 µL
   • Biotin‑CD45R/B220 0.5 mg/mL – 50 µL
   • Biotin‑CD127 0.5 mg/mL – 50 µL
   • Sterile PBS – 350 µL
   Total volume 700 µL.
   Use 3 µL of this master mix for every 1 × 10⁷ cells.
Incubate the cells with the lineage cocktail for 30 min on ice in the dark (titrate each antibody beforehand).
Wash with 5 mL cold PBS and centrifuge at 440 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

Add fluorochrome‑conjugated antibodies at the following dilutions:
   • Streptavidin‑APC‑eFluor 780 (1:400)
   • APC‑c‑Kit (1:400)
   • PE‑Sca‑1 (1:400)
   • PE/Cy7‑CD150 (1:400)
   • FITC‑CD34 (1:100)
   • BV510‑CD45 (1:400)
Incubate on ice in the dark for 90 min (critical for optimal CD34 staining).

steps.title: Configure cytometer and acquire samples
steps.instruction: Warm up the flow cytometer, perform performance validation, set compensation and voltages, add PI, acquire data at ≤5 000 events/s while keeping samples on ice, and apply the sequential gating strategy to record HSCs.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the flow cytometer and allow lasers to warm up for at least 30 min.
Run CS&T beads for performance validation.
Set up compensation using single‑stained controls (use cells for all markers except rare antigens).
Verify the compensation matrix accuracy.
Set FSC and SSC voltages using unstained cells.
Confirm positive/negative population separation using Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls.
Add Propidium Iodide to a final concentration of 0.1 % immediately before analysis.
Acquire samples, maintaining an acquisition rate below 5 000 events/s; keep samples on ice throughout.

Apply the sequential gating strategy (Figure 2):
   1. FSC‑A vs. SSC‑A to identify cells.
   2. FSC‑A vs. FSC‑H and SSC‑A vs. SSC‑W for doublet discrimination.
   3. PI‑negative (live) cells.
   4. CD45⁺ hematopoietic cells.
   5. Lineage‑negative cells.
   6. c‑Kit⁺ Sca‑1⁺ (KSL) cells.
   7. CD34⁻ CD150⁺ KSL HSCs.
   Record the events.
Stained samples may be kept on ice in FACS buffer for up to 1 h before acquisition.

steps.title: Analyze flow data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Use FlowJo software to apply the gating hierarchy, calculate population frequencies and absolute cell numbers, repeat the experiment at least three times, present data as mean ± SEM, and apply appropriate statistical tests for group comparisons.
